q: 1. In a precision traverse, included angles are measured by setting the vernier ...............
options: to read zero exactly on back station
to read 5° exactly on back station
somewhere near zero and reading both verniers on back station
explain: In high-precision work, instead of setting to exactly zero, it's better to read the actual initial readings on both verniers to eliminate setting errors.

q: 2. When the length of chain used in measuring distance is longer than the standard length, the error in measured distance will be ...............
explain: If the chain is too long, it measures a shorter distance than actual, resulting in a negative error (Correction is positive).

q: 3. Greater accuracy in linear measurements, is obtained by ...............
explain: Invar tapes have a very low coefficient of thermal expansion, making them the most accurate for baseline measurements.

q: 4. Subtense tacheometry is generally preferred to if ground is ...............
explain: The subtense bar method is particularly useful in rough or undulating terrain where chaining is difficult or impossible.

q: 5. Cross staff is an instrument used for ...............
explain: A cross-staff is a simple instrument used in chain surveying to set out perpendicular offsets (right angles) from the chain line.

q: 6. An invar tape is made of an alloy of ...............
explain: Invar is an alloy consisting of approximately 36% nickel and 64% steel.

q: 7. The Simpson's rule of areas assumes that the portions of the boundary between the ends of ordinates are ...............
explain: Simpson's rule (Prismoidal rule) is based on the assumption that the boundary is a second-degree curve (parabola).

q: 8. The fundamental principle of surveying is to work from the ...............
explain: Working from 'whole to part' prevents the accumulation of errors by localizing them within small areas.

q: 9. An angle of 45° with a chain line may be set out with
explain: A French cross staff is octagonal with slits cut at 45°, allowing for the setting out of both 45° and 90° angles.

q: 10. Pick up the most accurate statement from the following
options: survey lines in an area should be as many as possible
number of base lines in an area is limited to one
main chain lines should form well conditioned triangles
oblique offsets are inferior to perpendicular offsets
explain: A well-conditioned triangle (angles between 30° and 120°) ensures that any errors in measurement have the least possible effect on the plotted position of points.

q: 11. A 30 m chain after measuring a distance of 6000 m was found to be 10 cm more than the designated length. If the chain was standardized before the commencement of survey then the true length is
explain: Average error = (0 + 10)/2 = 5 cm. True distance = Measured distance * (Actual length / Design length). $6000 * (30.05 / 30) = 6010$ m.

q: 12. A chain is made up of mild steel or galvanized iron wire of diameter
explain: Standard metric chains are constructed from 4 mm diameter galvanized mild steel wire.

q: 13. An invar tape is generally used... because it possesses ___ coefficient of thermal expansion.
explain: Invar (an alloy of nickel and steel) has an extremely low coefficient of thermal expansion, making it highly stable during temperature changes.

q: 14. It is more convenient and gives better results while measuring horizontal distance ___ by stepping method.
explain: Chaining downhill is more accurate because the surveyor can hold the chain horizontal and drop a plumb bob more easily and steadily.

q: 15. In a whole circle system, the bearing of a line is measured
options: always clockwise from the south point
clockwise or anticlockwise from the east or west
clockwise or anticlockwise from the north or south
explain: In WCB, the bearing is always measured clockwise from the North point only. None of the listed options accurately describe this.

q: 16. Surveys which are carried out to depict mountains, rivers... are known as
explain: Topographical surveys are used to determine the natural features of a country (mountains, rivers, lakes) and artificial features (roads, canals).

q: 17. The length of a link of Gunter's chain is
explain: A Gunter's chain is 66 feet long with 100 links. Each link is $66/100 = 0.66$ feet long.

q: 18. Survey is conducted at 40° C and the measured length was 5 km. If the chain was standardized at 20° C and co-efficient of linear expansion... is 0.3 x 10^-5/°C, then the correct length is
explain: Correction for temperature $C_t = L alpha (T_m - T_s)$. Here, $5000 	imes 0.000003 	imes (40-20) = 0.30$ m. Since $T_m > T_s$, the correction is positive. True length = $5000 + 0.30 = 5000.30$ m.

q: 19. The maximum tolerance in 20 m chain is
explain: According to standard specifications, the permissible error for a 20 m metric chain is $pm 5$ mm.

q: 20. For accurate work, the steel band should always be used in preference to chain because the steel band
options: is practically inextensible and is not liable to kinks
can be easily repaired in the field
explain: Steel bands (or tapes) are superior to link chains because they do not stretch (inextensible) and do not have the hundreds of joints that can wear out or trap dirt.

q: 21. In case of a direct vernier scale
options: smallest division is longer than smallest division of the main scale
graduations increase in the same direction
explain: In a direct vernier, the scale graduations increase in the same direction as the main scale, and $n$ vernier divisions equal $(n-1)$ main scale divisions.

q: 22. Cumulative error that occur in chaining are proportional to .............
explain: Cumulative errors (like incorrect tape length) increase directly with the length of the line (L), whereas compensating errors are proportional to √L.

q: 23. The main difference between an optical square and prism square is .............
options: that optical square is more accurate than prism square
that no adjustment is required in a prism square since the angle between the reflecting surfaces cannot be changed
explain: While both use the principle of double reflection, the prism square is fixed and requires no adjustment compared to the mirrors in an optical square.

q: 24. Measurements taken with a wrong scale can be corrected by using the relation
options: true length = (correct scale / wrong scale) × measured length
true length = (correct scale / wrong scale)² × measured length
true length = (correct scale / wrong scale)³ × measured length
explain: Linear correction is proportional to the ratio of the scales. For area, the ratio would be squared; for volume, cubed.

q: 25. If x is the smallest division on the main scale and n are the number of divisions on the vernier, then the least count of the vernier is
explain: The least count is the difference between the smallest division of the main scale and the vernier scale, which mathematically simplifies to $x/n$.

q: 26. Accuracy of elevation of various points obtained from contour map is limited to
explain: The standard acceptable error in interpolated elevations from a contour map is generally taken as half of the contour interval.

q: 27. The intercept of a staff
options: is maximum if the staff is held truly normal...
is minimum if the staff is held truly normal...
decreases if the staff is tilted away from normal
increases if the staff is tilted towards normal
explain: The staff intercept is at its mathematical minimum when the staff is held exactly normal (perpendicular) to the line of sight.

q: 28. If vertical angles of inclined sights do not exceed 10° and non-verticality of the staff remains within 1° stadia system...
options: staff normal as well as vertical
explain: For small vertical angles (under 10°), holding the staff vertical is the standard practice in stadia tacheometry as it simplifies the reduction of readings to horizontal distances.

q: 29. Prismatic compass is considered more accurate than a surveyor's compass, because
options: graduation are in whole circle bearings
explain: The prism allows the surveyor to read the graduated ring while simultaneously sighting the object, leading to higher precision and reduced observation error.

q: 30. The stadia intercept on a fixed hair instrument vertically held is 1 m. if its constraints are 800 and 0.5 and total number of turns are 16, the horizontal distance between the instrument and target is
explain: Using the formula $D = Ks + C$, where $K=100$ and $C=0.5$. If intercept $s=0.5$, then $D = (100 	imes 0.5) + 0.5 = 50.5$ meters.

q: 31. If a chain is used at a temperature .....the tempr at which it was calibrated one, the error in measured length is negative
explain: Heat causes the metal chain to expand (become longer). Since the chain is longer than it should be, it records a measurement smaller than the actual distance, resulting in a positive error (higher than expected).

q: 32. In profile leveling, staff readings on neighbouring pegs 20 m apart are 1.200 and 1.000... proposed road had a
explain: Difference in level = $1.200 - 1.000 = 0.200$ (Fall). Gradient = $0.2 / 20 = 1 / 100$ (Falling).

q: 33. Diurnal variation of magnetic declination is
options: less at equator than nearer the poles
explain: Diurnal (daily) variation is generally smaller at the equator and increases as you move toward the magnetic poles.

q: 34. The position of point can be fixed more accurately by .............
explain: Perpendicular offsets are generally more accurate and easier to plot than oblique offsets because they provide the shortest distance from the chain line to the object.

q: 35. A 20 m long chain when should not show an error exceeding .............
options: 2 mm per meter length and 5 mm in the overall length
2 mm per meter length and 8 mm in the overall length
2 mm per meter length and 20 mm in the overall length
2 mm per meter length and 40 mm in the overall length
explain: Standard tolerance for a 20m chain is ±5mm, while for a 30m chain it is ±8mm.

q: 36. If the length of a chain line along a slope of θ° is l, the required slope correction is .............
explain: The correction is $l(1 - \cos \theta)$, which simplifies using trigonometric identity $1 - \cos \theta = 2 \sin^2 (\theta/2)$.

q: 37. A tape of length l and weight W kg/m is suspended at its ends with a pull of p kg, the sag correction is .............
explain: The standard formula for sag correction is $C_s =  rac{W^2 L}{24 P^2}$, where $W$ is the total weight ($w 	imes L$). If $W$ is weight per unit length, the formula is $ rac{w^2 L^3}{24 P^2}$.

q: 38. Accidental or compensating errors of length L are proportional to .............
explain: According to the law of probability, accidental errors (which are as likely to be positive as negative) tend to increase in proportion to the square root of the number of observations or length.

q: 39. While measuring a chain line between two stations A and B intervened by a raised ground .............
options: both vision and chaining get obstructed
explain: Raised ground primarily obstructs vision (intervisibility), necessitating indirect ranging, although the actual physical chaining (measurement) might still be possible.

q: 40. Prolongation of chain line across an obstruction chain surveying, is done by .............
explain: In pure chain surveying (without a theodolite), obstructions are bypassed using geometric constructions like perpendiculars or parallel lines created only with the chain.

q: 41. In chain surveying field work is limited to .............
explain: The defining characteristic of chain surveying is that only linear measurements (distances) are taken in the field.

q: 42. If L is the distance between two supports from which a tape is suspended under a pull P. If W is the total weight of the tape the sag correction is .............
explain: The standard formula for sag correction when using the total weight W is $C_s =  rac{W^2 L}{24 P^2}$.

q: 43. You have to observe an included angle with better accuracy than what is achievable by a vernier, you will prefer the method of .............
explain: The method of repetition allows the same angle to be measured multiple times and divided by the number of repetitions, which reduces the least-count error.

q: 44. Correct length of a 50 m tape, weighing 1.2 kg when a pull of 12 kg is applied at the ends and is freely suspended is .............
explain: Using the sag correction formula $ rac{W^2 L}{24 P^2} =  rac{1.2^2 	imes 50}{24 	imes 12^2} =  rac{72}{3456} ≈ 0.02$m. Corrected length = $50 - 0.02 = 49.98$ m.

q: 45. If a 30 m chain diverges through a perpendicular distance from its correct alignment, the error in length is .............
explain: The error due to bad alignment is approximately $d^2 / 2L$. For a 30m chain, this becomes $d^2 / (2 	imes 30) = d^2 / 60$.
